notes: MEASUREMENT (no claim-status change; advances L1). Headline: the Ollama 6th concurrent exchange QUEUES and succeeds (no failure); the 7th-16th also queue-and-succeed; a hard failure exists but it is a 429 Too Many Requests that first appeared at N=20 (2 of 20), not at 6. The '~5' belief is too conservative for glm-5.2:cloud; the queue-then-429 threshold is ~18-20 concurrent exchanges against a ~3-session background and is load-dependent, not a fixed wall. Evidence (tool-written): docs/evidence/OLLAMA-CONC/ — heartbeat-excerpt.jsonl (71 lines, per-worker finish ts + true wall), per-worker-table.tsv (heartbeat wall joined with OS rc/answer/429), driver-summaries.json (fleet pre/post snapshots), 429-error-samples.txt, PROVENANCE.md. Method: N concurrent one-shot `ollama run glm-5.2:cloud` at N=4,5,6,8,12,16,20, each wrapped in tools/runner with a distinct MANAGENT_TASK_ID=T357-w<id>-<label> so untracked/heartbeat.jsonl records tool-written per-worker finish ts + true wall. Baseline single-request latency 1.4s. Per-N (N tried / succeeded / 429-failed; heartbeat walls sorted, seconds): N=4 -> 4/4/0 [1.8,2.2,2.6,3.4]; N=5 -> 5/5/0 [1.4,1.4,1.7,2.3,3.8]; N=6 -> 6/6/0 [2.0,2.8,3.5,4.2,4.8,5.5] (the 6th waits ~4s, succeeds); N=8 -> 8/8/0 [6.6..9.6]; N=12 -> 12/12/0 [1.1..6.9]; N=16 -> 16/16/0 [2.0..10.0]; N=20 -> 18/20/2 (429, fail walls 0.2,0.3). Answers to the brief's five questions: (1) the 6th QUEUES, succeeds; not a connection error. (2) wait grows with N (median 1.4s->5.5s->5.9s->8s+); staircase of grouped finishes ~ a small number (~2-3 against background) of concurrent service slots draining a queue, NOT a single strictly-ordered FIFO queue; ordering NOT conclusively proved (launch order not tagged tightly) — UNSETTLED. (3) the 429 is detectable: ollama run exits rc=1 with `Error: 429 Too Many Requests: too many concurrent requests` on stderr (429-error-samples.txt); bin/ollama-subagent's dispatch_verify.heal_dispatch (tools/dispatch_verify.py:296) on rc!=0 with row in_progress runs `managent reopen` -> row returns to dispatchable; so a 429-killed dispatch would NOT leave a claimed row with a dead worker — but this is a CODE-READ INFERENCE + observed 429 rc, NOT a live end-to-end trace of a real bin/ollama-subagent 429->heal (deliberately not induced live against the running fleet). (4) leans toward counting SIMULTANEOUS ACTIVE EXCHANGES not live sessions (3 live-but-mostly-idle persistent sessions throughout did not block 20 one-shots until ~2 hit 429), but NOT cleanly settled — needs the controlled K-idle + M-active matrix on a QUIET fleet, which this run did not have. (5) practical cap for long-thinking workers is materially higher than ~5: each worker holds an active-exchange slot only while streaming (seconds), then idles for minutes while thinking; the 429 only bites when simultaneous active exchanges reach ~18-20; idle-thinking workers don't count, so the binding constraint is PEAK CONCURRENT STREAMING, not worker headcount. DEVIATION from the brief (documented in PROVENANCE.md + report): used `ollama run` one-shots wrapped in tools/runner instead of bin/ollama-subagent, because bin/ollama-subagent launches full persistent pi agents that think 10+ min, would occupy the slots being measured, risk wall-kill, and clobber the live kanban; the Ollama concurrency limit is a server/cloud property observable by any concurrent Ollama request, and the brief's required evidence (heartbeat file + exit statuses) is preserved. CAVEAT: the fleet was NOT quiet — 3 live persistent ollama launch pi sessions (T353 active ~9% CPU, T357=this, T362) ran throughout; all numbers are residual capacity against that background; the operator dispatched T352/T362 during the run, so the quiet-fleet precondition was not given. The one follow-up that tightens every number: re-measure on a drained fleet, including the K-idle+M-active matrix to settle question (4). No dispatch-policy change (brief forbade it); the scheduling ruling is the operator's.
